---
title: "Design tokens"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8.8, fig.height = 4.4, dpi = 100,
  fig.retina = 2, dev = "ragg_png", out.width = "100%"
)
options(gglaplot2.font = "inter")
library(ggplot2)
library(gglaplot2)
```

A design token is a named decision: `text` is the colour body text is set in,
`chart-grid` the colour of a gridline, `data-primary` the colour of the first
series. The visualisation team keeps the tokens in Figma and publishes them as
a package; this package vendors the published Sass unchanged under
`inst/tokens/` and generates `gla_tokens` from it, so nothing in R carries a
colour typed by hand. Every token has a light value and a dark value.

```{r}
head(gla_tokens)
nrow(gla_tokens)
```

## Reading a token

`gla_token()` reads one or several by name, in either mode. An unknown name
is an error, so a typo fails at the call rather than surfacing as a missing
colour on a chart.

```{r}
gla_token("data-primary")
gla_token(c("chart-axis", "chart-grid"), theme = "dark")
```

## The groups a chart uses

The `chart-*` group is the non-data ink: surface, gridlines, axis, labels.
`theme_gla()` is built from it.

```{r chart-tokens, fig.height = 4}
gla_show_tokens("^chart-")
```

The `data-*` group is what data is drawn in. `data-primary`, `data-secondary`
and `data-tertiary` are the first three series; `data-context` is the grey a
comparator is drawn in; `data-positive` and `data-negative` colour a rise and a
fall; `data-female` and `data-male` a split by sex; `data-empty` a missing
value.

```{r data-tokens, fig.height = 7.5}
gla_show_tokens("^data-")
```

The `palette-*` ramps are the steps the sequential and diverging palettes are
interpolated from.

```{r palette-tokens, fig.height = 4}
gla_show_tokens("^palette-blue-")
```

## Brand colours

`gla_brand` holds the twelve brand statics. They are identity colours, for a
logo or a masthead, and not for data: the `data-*` tokens are chosen for
separability and contrast on a chart.

```{r}
gla_brand
```

## Refreshing

When the visualisation team release a new token package, drop the new
`_colors.scss` and `_primitives.scss` into `inst/tokens/` and run
`data-raw/tokens.R`. A test checks the data against the vendored file, so a
refresh that was not regenerated fails the suite. The Rhino dashboard template
vendors the same two files; a refresh is done in both from the same release.
